did.abstract: Photographs, documents and clippings documenting the blessing of the Thunderbird mosaic at the Pierrepont playground in Brooklyn Heights on April 8, 1995.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This small collection is housed in a single folder with no particular arrangement.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: In 1993, Parks Department gardener John Colletti created a 30-by-20 foot cobblestone mosaic in the shape of a bird. The design was inspired by a book on American Indians, and about 800 cobblestones, purchased in Coney Island, were used to create it. The mosaic was located in a flower garden along the Brooklyn Heights Promenade. In 1995, the City Arts Commission approved an expansion of the adjacent Pierrepont Playground into the space occupied by the mosaic. Parks Commissioner Henry Stern proposed that the mosaic be moved to a different site at the north end of the Promenade near Orange Street and Columbia Heights. Colletti's friend Chris Roberts, an American Indian advocate, organized a blessing ceremony prior to the mosaic's relocation, which was held on April 8, 1995. Though the mosaic is not an authentic relic, the organizers stated that they wanted to "legitimize" the piece before its relocation.

Clinton Elliot, a Chippewa Indian, conducted the blessing at sunrise. Elliott was then treasurer of the Board of Directors of American Indian Community House (AICH), and also worked as a producer of films and videos for the Museum of the American Indian. He is also known as Wasswanin, or Torch Bearer.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The photographs in this collection were initially added to the Brooklyn photograph and illustration collection (ARC.202) under the subject heading Brooklyn Heights. In 2026, the documents and clippings were found in collection by Dee Bowers and subsequently reunited with the photographs to create this collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: 10 color 4x6" photographs, 1 press release, 1 photocopy of special event permit, 1 biography of Clinton C. Elliott, and 4 newspaper articles documenting the blessing of the Thunderbird mosaic at the Pierrepont playground on April 8, 1995. The photographs depict Elliott, Chris Roberts, and John Colletti; Elliott performing the ceremony; and community members there to watch the ceremony.
